quotes.text: This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Funds settle in your Stripe balance in USD.
Your customers can use stablecoins as payment globally, but only US businesses can accept stablecoin payments.
Stripe reviews your access request and contact you for more details if necessary. The payment method appears as **Pending** while we review your request.

If you use Stripe’s default [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) with Payment Links, Hosted Checkout, Embedded Checkout Forms, or Elements, then you don’t need to make any further updates.
You can create crypto payments in the currencies that map to your country. The default local currency for crypto is USD, with customers also seeing their purchase amount in this currency.

findings: The 2026-11-07 base capture is a 20-line variant index (new raw:9-20), whereas the matched old capture bundles detailed Checkout, two Elements API routes, Direct API, iOS, and Android sections (old raw:29-37,126-128,669-671,1344-1348,1635-1641,1939-1945). Their absence from the new base capture is a rendering/navigation change, not evidence that those options were discontinued; no variant content was fetched in this job.

Mapped source:13 says there are only three integration paths. The old bundled guide and new index both identify Direct API and mobile iOS/Android routes. Correct the source path inventory with explicit dated/index provenance; preserve the old full guide as factual raw evidence and do not add the index-only capture to factual raw_files.

Mapped source:19 states unqualified no-code automatic crypto display. Old raw:17-23 ties use to a requested, reviewed, active merchant payment method and to default dynamic payment methods with named integrations; customer eligibility is separate. Scope the source sentence accordingly, without implying live merchant or customer eligibility from a dated capture.

Mapped source:21 and :25 describe USD in specific Checkout and PaymentIntent examples. Old raw:37 requires USD Checkout line items for that path, old raw:1522 permits crypto payment currencies mapping to merchant country with USD as default in Direct API, and old raw:8 says settlement reaches the Stripe balance in USD. Keep payer stablecoin, API/payment currency, line-item currency, and Stripe-balance settlement as distinct facts; do not generalize USD line items to every route.

Concept:53 and Stripe index:239 repeat the incomplete path inventory. If the source correction is approved, align those navigation summaries with the same historical qualification; the concept's US-merchant and USD-settlement claims at :10-12 are from its other primary source and this index does not independently refresh them.
substantive_changes: No new operating, eligibility, token, network, currency, or settlement terms can be inferred from the new base capture; it supplies variant URLs only.

The new index makes six routes explicit (new raw:13,15-20), including Direct API and iOS/Android routes omitted by the mapped source's three-path summary. This is a navigation/discoverability correction grounded also in the old detailed capture.
historical_claims_to_preserve: At the date of the old capture, the guide restricted merchant acceptance to US businesses while describing global customer payment (old raw:12), and required Dashboard request/review/approval before the method became active (old raw:17-19).

At the date of the old capture, stablecoin customer payment redirected to crypto.stripe.com and funds settled in the merchant Stripe balance in USD (old raw:8); these are different from payment or line-item currency.

Keep the old detailed Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS, Android, testnet, and code examples as dated evidence; the 2026-11-07 index does not supersede their content or establish that those examples still execute.
conflicts: Source:13 and concept:53/index:239 describe only Checkout and Elements/PaymentIntents paths, while new raw:17,19-20 and old raw:1344-1348,1635-1641,1939-1945 also show Direct API and mobile paths.
Source:19 omits the merchant approval and default-dynamic-methods conditions in old raw:17-23; its wording could be read as universally automatic.

A universal USD payment-currency interpretation of source:21,25 would conflict with old raw:1522's country-mapped Direct API currencies; source:21's USD line-item requirement is specific to its Checkout example.
unresolved_questions: The 2026-11-07 variant destinations were not captured in this job. Their current detailed instructions, account/geographic availability, and supported payment currencies remain unverified here.
The dated guide and index do not establish approval, eligibility, successful payment, blockchain finality, or settlement for any specific live account or transaction.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/accept-stablecoin-payments, the 2026-11-07 capture is a variant index (new raw:9-20), not a replacement detailed integration guide. It lists Checkout, two Elements API choices, Direct API, iOS, and Android. The old capture contains the underlying detailed sections (old raw:29-37,1344-1348,1635-1641,1939-1945). [[source-stripe-accept-stablecoin-payments]] should preserve the dated old guide and correct its three-path inventory; no route's omission from the new base text proves deprecation.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/accept-stablecoin-payments, [[source-stripe-accept-stablecoin-payments]] should qualify automatic display by prior merchant request and approval plus use of default dynamic payment methods in the named integrations (old raw:17-23; source:17-19). Its Checkout USD line-item instruction is route-specific (old raw:33-37); Direct API payment currencies map to merchant country with USD default (old raw:1520-1522), while Stripe-balance settlement was USD in the dated guide (old raw:8). New raw:11-20 supplies navigation only, so it cannot verify present eligibility or live settlement.
